name: James
description: Man living at the time of the New Testament

points: Is not this the carpenter's son? His brethren James, Joses, Simon and Judas, and his sisters, are all with us; James wrote James and Judas wrote Jude, and they were his brothers.

note.label: The Nativity: the Bloodline, Birthright, & the Messiah

points: Is not this the carpenter's son? is not his mother called Mary? and his brethren, James, and Joses, and Simon, and Judas, and his sisters, are they not all with us? Mary did not just have Jesus; she had other children. The Zondervan compact Bible dictionary entry on Mary lists the distinctive Roman Catholic doctrines about her, the immaculate conception and the assumption of Mary, and we just showed in the scriptures that the perpetual virginity claim is a lie.

note.label: In Vain Do They Worship Me! Religious Syncretism

points: In his own country they are astonished and ask, Is not this the carpenter's son? They name his mother, his brethren James, Joses, Simon and Judas, and his sisters, all of them living among them.

note.label: Matthew 13: The Parables of the Kingdom

points: Paul identifies which apostles he saw when he went to Jerusalem: only Peter and James the Lord's brother. He swears before God that he is telling the truth about his history and his calling.

note.label: Galatians 1: Paul's Apostleship and the True Gospel

points: James, Cephas, and John gave Paul and Barnabas the right hands of fellowship; that we should go unto the heathen, and they unto the circumcision. The heathen: talking about the northern kingdom.

note.label: Acts 10 Reloaded: Call No Man Common

points: They saw that the gospel of the uncircumcision was committed unto me, as the gospel of the circumcision was unto Peter, for he that wrought effectually in Peter to the apostleship of the circumcision, the same was mighty in me toward the Gentiles. Christ worked in Peter toward the Jews born and raised in the law and circumcised the eighth day, and the same Christ worked in Paul toward the dispersed. James, Cephas, and John gave the right hands of fellowship that we should go unto the heathen and they unto the circumcision, remembering the poor.

note.label: Navigating Through Paul's Letters: Walking Through Galatians

points: But when Peter was come to Antioch, I withstood him to the face, because he was to be blamed. Before certain came from James, he did eat with the Gentiles: but when they were come, he withdrew and separated himself, fearing them which were of the circumcision. Paul said: you already learned this, Peter; God showed you that you cannot call any man common or unclean. You sat with them; you convinced many of the Jews that these men were all right. But now you are wavering.

note.label: Acts 10 Reloaded: Call No Man Common

points: Before certain men came from James, Peter ate with the Gentiles (Israelites living in a Gentile way of life). But when the southern kingdom arrived, Peter withdrew and separated himself from the northern kingdom out of respect of persons.

note.label: Galatians 2: The Council at Jerusalem and Justification by Faith

points: James, a servant of God, to the twelve tribes which are scattered abroad. My brethren, count it all joy when ye fall into divers temptations. Why would you count it joy to fall into temptations? Answers from the floor: because the Lord sees you fit to be chastised and you will be increased; because being tried reaffirms you are a son of God; because you are learning about yourself, learning your faults. That last one is the point: you count it joy because you are learning what you have to fix.

note.label: Listen, Learn & Live The Art of Enduring in The Truth

points: James, a servant of God, to the twelve tribes which are scattered abroad. So Paul and James are on one accord. Then how is it that they claim Paul taught not to keep the commandments, but they never accuse James of that?

note.label: In Vain Do They Worship Me! Religious Syncretism

points: James writes to the twelve tribes which are scattered abroad. Even in the New Testament it tells you the twelve tribes were scattered; they would not be sitting in the land of Israel.
